newsitem.title: USA: Holbrooke says new peace force needed in Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: Holbrooke says new peace force needed in Bosnia.

text.p: Failure to put another NATO peacekeeping force in Bosnia next year would risk new warfare there, former Bosnia peace negotiator Richard Holbrooke said on Tuesday.
"You can't go from 60,000 (present NATO peacekeepers) to zero without an implosion," Holbrooke said at a Senate Foreign Relations subcommittee hearing, adding later: "The war could even resume."

Holbrooke was chief architect of last year's peace accord that came from intensive closed-door U.S.-sponsored negotiations in Dayton, Ohio. NATO peacekeepers have enforced the pact, but have been scheduled to leave in December.
Holbrooke said the new force need not be as large as the present one and said he was confident another group of peacekeepers will be sent, ensuring that peace in Bosnia will be maintained.

Defence Secretary William Perry said after a meeting of NATO defence ministers in Bergen, Norway, last week that the United States will strongly consider contributing U.S. troops to a new force if NATO decides one is needed.
Holbrooke said Europeans were willing to send more troops but said they insisted the United States supply some of the troops.
"On the economic side, I am more troubled," Holbrooke said. "I believe that the United States should be trying to do a little more to show leadership here."
He said Bosnia needed a central bank and central government agencies to restore the country's economy and promote foreign trade -- along with police and other government agencies.
"These things will only happen if they're pushed by external forces, led by the United States," he said.
